newsitem.title: UK: BA signs Latam-Caribbean cargo contract.
newsitem.headline: BA signs Latam-Caribbean cargo contract.

text.p: British Airways World Cargo has signed a contract with new cargo carrier Cargo Link Caribbean Ltd to transport freight between Britain and Latin America via Barbados, BA's outsourced capacity cargo manager Graham Bunsell said on Friday.

"We operate up to six weekly London Gatwick-Barbados flights with passenger Boeing 747-200s. As this is primarily a passenger route, the available bellyhold cargo capacity is under-utilised," he told Reuters.
"Cargo Link's new services based on its Bridgetown hub have given us an opportunity to feed traffic to and from Latin America on its flights," he said.

Bunsell added that BA World Cargo was currently mainly using Cargo Link's Chile-Bridgetown capacity to feed its London-bound flights, although freight from Peru was also being generated as a result of the link-up.
"Outbound from Britain to South America via the Cargo Link connection has yet to be really developed but we are looking to expand this operation in both directions," he said.

Cargo Link Caribbean, registered in Barbados, was formed in November and operates a wet-leaed 43-tonne DC-8-54 freighter between Bridgetown and Latin American airports. Wet-leasing covers the hire of both aircraft and crew.
